scope: Local implementation only; persistent mode requires pending SQL migration
specificTests: CPU close preserves cards/history, closes open turn, increments version and awards opponent
close rejects foreign identities, stale version and reused key; concurrent retry closes once
create requires consent; confirmed exact CPU closes atomically and retry cannot close a newer game
failed create rolls back CPU closure and receipt even after closure hook ran
join replaces CPU for guest, host starts and both hands stay private
invalid, expired, full or wrong-size rooms never close CPU; throttling persists
two guests racing: only winner closes CPU; losing guest retains their exact state
failed join after closure hook rolls back the old game, new game and receipt
CPU worker racing with close is version-safe and cannot revive a closed game
switch cannot close an online or foreign game; plain online abandon still closes room
old finished target never overwrites a different current CPU; all operations rollback
helper execution remains private and table RLS/counts are unchanged

semantics.roomTransition: Explicit exact own CPU ID; close and room operation atomic
semantics.uncertainRetry: same requestId and confirmed target preserved

limits: Supabase shared database unchanged; pending migration needed before persistent feature works there
SQL tests use real isolated PostgreSQL; browser flows and HTTP Auth/RPC use controlled fixtures
No real user profile/game changed; previous local SQL/diagram deliveries preserved
